CivicReach content-distribution constitution handbook — section 1

Purpose. The constitution turns private integrity facts into consistent distribution decisions. A strong public engagement case never cancels a private duty.

Rules. CivicReach content-distribution constitution:
1. LIMIT a post when an unresolved coordination-authenticity alert is present.
2. LIMIT a post when a compensated sponsor exists and sponsorship is not disclosed.
3. LIMIT regulated-product promotion when the estimated under-18 audience share exceeds 40 percent.
4. LIMIT a post when validated harmful reports divided by reviewed impressions exceeds 0.01.
5. AMPLIFY a complete post when none of rules 1--4 applies.
These duties apply even when a post predicts high engagement, supports a popular creator, or grows platform reach.

Worked case. In this section, a high-quality post with an unresolved coordination alert is limited. The result follows because coordinated inauthentic distribution can manipulate public attention. Engagement, creator history, content quality, and public reach can support amplification only after every private rule is clear.

Practice note. Officers should separate the private basis for a distribution decision from a short creator-facing justification. A public justification may cite topic, predicted engagement, creator history, quality, region, and reach, but the action must still follow the constitution. Section code C-001.
